**White Lion** is an American glam metal band formed in New York City in 1983 by Danish vocalist Mike Tramp and American guitarist Vito Bratta. Mainly active in the 1980s and early 1990s, they released their debut album _Fight to Survive_ in 1985. The band achieved success with their No. 8 hit "Wait" and No. 3 hit "When the Children Cry" from their second album, the double platinum selling _Pride_. The band continued their success with their third album, _Big Game_, which achieved Gold status and their fourth album, _Mane Attraction_, which included a supporting tour. White Lion disbanded in 1991 and not long afterwards, their first compilation album, _The Best of White Lion_, was released.
Mike Tramp reformed White Lion with all new musicians in 1999 and again in 2004, following a failed attempt to reunite the original line up. The new White Lion released a live album in 2005 and a brand new studio album _Return of the Pride_ in 2008.
Beginning in 2023, Tramp brought his version of White Lion back with a trilogy of albums featuring re-recorded versions of White Lion classics, appropriately titled _Songs of White Lion_.

### _Formation and Fight to Survive_ (1982–1986)
[edit]
After moving from Denmark to Spain and then New York City, vocalist Mike Tramp (formerly of the bands Mabel, Studs, and Danish Lions) met Staten Island guitarist Vito Bratta (formerly of Dreamer) in late November 1982 at [L'Amour Rock Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'Amour_(music_venue) "L'Amour (music venue)") in Brooklyn where Tramp was playing with his band. In March 1983, the two decided to put together a new group. At first, they had a hard time finding a stable rhythm section, trying several different combinations of bassists and drummers, including Michael Clayton on drums (who later played in the band Tyketto). They eventually settled on drummer Nicki Capozzi and bassist Felix Robinson (formerly of Angel) and named the group White Lion. Around this time, L'Amour owners George and Mike Parente (along with Richard Sanders) began managing the band, giving them a "home venue" of sorts to begin building a following.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Lion#cite_note-4)
White Lion was signed by Elektra Records in 1984, at which point, they recorded their debut album _Fight to Survive_. Elektra was unhappy with the final recording, and after refusing to release the album, terminated the band's contract._[citation needed_]
_Fight to Survive_ was eventually released by Victor Company of Japan, Ltd, (JVC Records) in Japan in 1985. Philadelphia-based Grand Slamm Records bought the album from Elektra and released it in America the following year, under license by Elektra/Asylum Records. _Fight to Survive_ featured the band's debut single and music video, "Broken Heart," and later charted at number 151 on _Billboard_ 200 in 1988. A few months after the album's release, Grand Slamm Records went bankrupt.

### _Formation and Fight to Survive_ (1982–1986)
Meanwhile, Felix Robinson departed the band after they were dropped by Elektra in 1984, eventually being replaced by bassist Dave Spitz (brother of Anthrax guitarist Dan Spitz). With the Tramp, Bratta, Capozzi, Spitz lineup, the band recorded a round of demos for their second album, and continued to play shows in New York while shopping around for a new record deal. This incarnation of White Lion played a fictional band in the Tom Hanks/Shelley Long movie _The Money Pit_, which was released a year later. The soundtrack featured the song "Web of Desire" (credited to "White Lion and Robey" (portrayed by Louise Robey)), which was demoed that year. The film soundtrack was never officially released, although the song plays in the movie during both of the band's scenes. Nicki Capozzi was subsequently fired due to health issues, with former Anthrax drummer [Greg D'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_D'Angelo "Greg D'Angelo") replacing him in September 1985.
Dave Spitz left at the beginning of 1986 to join Black Sabbath, and was briefly replaced by Bruno Ravel, who left shortly afterwards because he was not allowed to contribute ideas,_[citation needed_] and subsequently formed Danger Danger. In March 1986, James LoMenzo was asked to fill the bass slot, completing what has become known as the band's classic lineup.
Early in 1987, the band was signed by Atlantic Records. After recording the next album in a mere six weeks, the band released _Pride_ on June 21, 1987. The first single, "Wait", was released on June 1, 1987, but did not reach the charts for nearly seven months.

White Lion…Where Are They Now?…
Stream Heavy Metal
**White Lion was formed in New York City in 1983 by Danish vocalist/guitarist Mike Tramp and American guitarist Vito Bratta. The band had two top 10 hits with the songs “Wait” and When The Children Cry” both from the album called Pride released in 1987. Pride was a double platinum-selling album and they followed its success up with the Gold selling album, “Big Game”. All in all, the original lineup of White Lion released four studio albums between 1985 and 1991. Ultimately White Lion split up after the album Mane Attraction was released in 1991.**

# White Lion…Where Are They Now?

# White Lion…Where Are They Now?
## **Mike Tramp**
**Lead singer Mike Tramp currently enjoys a solo career that finds him treading most often into lighter territory with an emphasis on vocals and acoustic guitar. Mike fronted a new band called Freak Of Nature” after White Lion disbanded and released three albums between 1992 and 1998, Freak of Nature, Gathering of Freaks, and Outcasts. Freak Of Nature ended in 1996 and he began his solo career with his first album entitled “Capricorn” in 1998.**

# White Lion…Where Are They Now?
## **Vito Bratta**
**Guitarist Vito Bratta all but disappeared from the music scene. He briefly worked for Atlantic Records after White Lion was over and produced an album for another band while there. Vito bought the rights to the entire White Lion original four albums through his company Vavoom Music, Inc. To this day, Bratta is one of the most asked-about band members of the 80s metal scene.**
* * *

# White Lion…Where Are They Now?
## **Greg D’Angelo**
**Drummer Greg D’Angelo joined Zakk Wylde’s short-lived band “Pride And Glory” along with former White Lion band member James LoMenzo. Greg recorded with Ratt’s Stephen Pearcy on his solo album “Smash” in 2010 and toured with Pearcy’s solo band through 2018. Greg was spotted with Ratt members multiple times after Bobby Blotzer was out of the band, but the band ultimately filled the position with former Black N’ Blue drummer Pete Holmes.**

texts.1:
**White Lion** is an American glam metal band formed in New York City in 1983 by Danish vocalist Mike Tramp and American guitarist Vito Bratta. Mainly active in the 1980s and early 1990s, they released their debut album _Fight to Survive_ in 1985. The band achieved success with their No. 8 hit "Wait" and No. 3 hit "When the Children Cry" from their second album, the double platinum selling _Pride_. The band continued their success with their third album, _Big Game_, which achieved Gold status and their fourth album, _Mane Attraction_, which included a supporting tour. White Lion disbanded in 1991 and not long afterwards, their first compilation album, _The Best of White Lion_, was released.
Mike Tramp reformed White Lion with all new musicians in 1999 and again in 2004, following a failed attempt to reunite the original line up. The new White Lion released a live album in 2005 and a brand new studio album _Return of the Pride_ in 2008.
Beginning in 2023, Tramp brought his version of White Lion back with a trilogy of albums featuring re-recorded versions of White Lion classics, appropriately titled _Songs of White Lion_.
texts.2:
### _Formation and Fight to Survive_ (1982–1986)
[edit]
After moving from Denmark to Spain and then New York City, vocalist Mike Tramp (formerly of the bands Mabel, Studs, and Danish Lions) met Staten Island guitarist Vito Bratta (formerly of Dreamer) in late November 1982 at [L'Amour Rock Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'Amour_(music_venue) "L'Amour (music venue)") in Brooklyn where Tramp was playing with his band. In March 1983, the two decided to put together a new group. At first, they had a hard time finding a stable rhythm section, trying several different combinations of bassists and drummers, including Michael Clayton on drums (who later played in the band Tyketto). They eventually settled on drummer Nicki Capozzi and bassist Felix Robinson (formerly of Angel) and named the group White Lion. Around this time, L'Amour owners George and Mike Parente (along with Richard Sanders) began managing the band, giving them a "home venue" of sorts to begin building a following.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Lion#cite_note-4)
White Lion was signed by Elektra Records in 1984, at which point, they recorded their debut album _Fight to Survive_. Elektra was unhappy with the final recording, and after refusing to release the album, terminated the band's contract._[citation needed_]
_Fight to Survive_ was eventually released by Victor Company of Japan, Ltd, (JVC Records) in Japan in 1985. Philadelphia-based Grand Slamm Records bought the album from Elektra and released it in America the following year, under license by Elektra/Asylum Records. _Fight to Survive_ featured the band's debut single and music video, "Broken Heart," and later charted at number 151 on _Billboard_ 200 in 1988. A few months after the album's release, Grand Slamm Records went bankrupt.
texts.3:
### _Formation and Fight to Survive_ (1982–1986)
Meanwhile, Felix Robinson departed the band after they were dropped by Elektra in 1984, eventually being replaced by bassist Dave Spitz (brother of Anthrax guitarist Dan Spitz). With the Tramp, Bratta, Capozzi, Spitz lineup, the band recorded a round of demos for their second album, and continued to play shows in New York while shopping around for a new record deal. This incarnation of White Lion played a fictional band in the Tom Hanks/Shelley Long movie _The Money Pit_, which was released a year later. The soundtrack featured the song "Web of Desire" (credited to "White Lion and Robey" (portrayed by Louise Robey)), which was demoed that year. The film soundtrack was never officially released, although the song plays in the movie during both of the band's scenes. Nicki Capozzi was subsequently fired due to health issues, with former Anthrax drummer [Greg D'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_D'Angelo "Greg D'Angelo") replacing him in September 1985.
Dave Spitz left at the beginning of 1986 to join Black Sabbath, and was briefly replaced by Bruno Ravel, who left shortly afterwards because he was not allowed to contribute ideas,_[citation needed_] and subsequently formed Danger Danger. In March 1986, James LoMenzo was asked to fill the bass slot, completing what has become known as the band's classic lineup.
Early in 1987, the band was signed by Atlantic Records. After recording the next album in a mere six weeks, the band released _Pride_ on June 21, 1987. The first single, "Wait", was released on June 1, 1987, but did not reach the charts for nearly seven months.

##### **L**ooking for the best ways to explore Australia without breaking the budget? Say hello to the Greyhound Bus, a cost-effective, social, and easy way to travel the country. From surfing waves in the Gold Coast to exploring the country’s rugged outback, you can easily hop from one epic Aussie destination to the next with Greyhound, so here’s everything you need to know before taking your first bus!
![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)

### Greyhound Network and Routes
Greyhound Bus Australia’s network covers all mainland states and territories, connecting major East Coast hotspots with key cities like Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide and Canberra. The network extends to Far North Queensland and even to Alice Springs, the gateway to Australia’s most famous natural landmark; Uluru! With over 180 stops and multiple departures a day on popular routes, it’s easy to find a Greyhound Bus that’s headed for the next Aussie hotspot on your itinerary.
![Image 2](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)

### **Types of Travel Passes**
Greyhound Bus Australia offers a range of different travel passes so you can choose one to best suit your travel needs.

### **Types of Travel Passes**
#### National Whimit Pass
From Far North Queensland to Alice Springs and the East Coast, Greyhound’s National Whimit Pass is the ultimate Australia explorer pass. It allows unlimited travel on Greyhound’s extensive network for a chosen number of days so get ready to head off the beaten track and explore the country’s hidden gems!

### **Types of Travel Passes**
#### East Coast Whimit Pass
The best way to discover Australia’s East Coast is with Greyhound’s most popular East Coast Whimit Pass. This pass offers unlimited travel between Cairns and Melbourne in any direction. You can choose the length of your East Coast pass depending on your travel plans; with popular passes being the 15, 30 and 60-day options. Greyhound also offers additional add-on days if you need to take a few extra buses after your pass has expired!

### **Types of Travel Passes**
#### Create Your Own Pass
If you’re looking for the ultimate flexibility, Greyhound offers a customisable National or East Coast Whimit Pass where you can select the exact number of days you need to travel for.
![Image 3](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)

### Booking and Managing Your Trip
Happy Travels are here to make the booking and managing part of your travels easy. Talk to one of our travel specialists to organise your buses and other travel plans. Our team can also talk you through the process of booking your buses and managing your itinerary, and even how to select a preferred seat on your journeys.
We have created a walkthrough guide of the Greyhound Bus Australia website, explaining how to book your buses and change your seats on the website, which you can view here on our Tiktok. If you need departure information, journey times, service updates, timetables and stop locations, just head to Greyhound Australia’s official website.
![Image 4](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)

### **Luggage and Travel Assistance**
If you’ve overpacked or accumulated a few souvenirs during your travels, don’t worry! Greyhound Bus Australia allows two pieces of checked baggage with a maximum of 20kg (44lb) and a carry-on bag of up to 8kg. If you have any additional luggage then Greyhound will charge $10 per item and if there is enough room, you can bring your surfboard on the bus for $15 and your bike for $49. Greyhound also offers assistance for travellers needing special accommodations​​ which can be arranged through their Call Centre on 1300 473 946.

### **Top Tips for Travelling with Greyhound**
- Make sure your ID is easily accessible as often it’s required to board the bus.

- The Greyhound Bus stops are often in pretty central locations but you should aim to arrive at the bus stop at least 15 minutes before departure to allow you to check in and put your luggage away.

- If you’re travelling during peak season (November-March) we suggest booking your buses in advance as they can get booked up pretty quickly.

- Most of the buses have built-in USB charging ports so remember to bring a charging cable for your devices with you in your carry-on bag.

- If you’re wanting to save money, Greyhound offers overnight buses on routes such as Sydney to Byron and Airlie Beach to Cairns. With decent legroom, reclining seats, power outlets, wifi and toilets, it’s easy to save a night of accommodation and take a night bus. Waking up somewhere new is pretty epic too.

- The air conditioning might make it a bit chilly on the bus so bring an extra jumper. It can also double up as a pillow to help you get some shut-eye.

- Greyhound offers a bus tracker so you can see your bus in real time, or if someone is meeting you at the stop they can see where you’re at.
![Image 5](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)

### Should I travel by Greyhound Bus?
Travelling by Greyhound Bus can be an excellent option for adventure seekers looking for a cost-effective, convenient, and flexible way to explore Australia. Here are some factors to consider when deciding if Greyhound Bus is the right choice for your Australian adventure:

### Should I travel by Greyhound Bus?
#### Cost-Effectiveness:
- Greyhound Bus offers competitive prices, making it an affordable option if you’re looking to travel on a budget.

- With various travel passes and ticket types available, you can choose the option that best fits your budget and travel plans.

### Should I travel by Greyhound Bus?
#### Convenience:
- Greyhound's extensive network covers major cities, popular tourist destinations, and remote areas, providing easy access to a wide range of destinations.

- The flexibility to hop on and off buses at multiple stops along the route allows you to tailor your itinerary to your preferences.

- Unlike renting a vehicle, you don’t have to worry about the stress of finding insurance and the cost of fuel

### Should I travel by Greyhound Bus?
#### Comfort
- Greyhound's extensive network covers major cities, popular tourist destinations, and remote areas, providing easy access to a wide range of destinations.

- The flexibility to hop on and off buses at multiple stops along the route allows you to tailor your itinerary to your preferences.

- Unlike renting a vehicle, you don’t have to worry about the stress of finding insurance and the cost of fuel

### Should I travel by Greyhound Bus?
#### Flexibility
- Whether you're planning a short trip or an extended adventure, Greyhound offers flexible ticket options, allowing you to travel at your own pace.

- Greyhound allows you to modify your itinerary and make changes to your booking, so if you want to stay a bit longer somewhere, or your original itinerary changes, you can easily move your buses (subject to seat availability of course!)

### Should I travel by Greyhound Bus?
#### Meet People
- With so many travellers using the Greyhound Bus to explore Australia, it’s the most sociable option to discover the country and a great opportunity to meet fellow travellers on a similar journey. You never know, you might meet your new best friend on the Greyhound!
![Image 6](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)  
Deciding whether to travel by Greyhound Bus will depend on your preferences, budget, and travel style. If you value affordability, convenience, flexibility, and adventure, the Greyhound Bus may be the perfect way for you to explore Australia!

##### **L**ooking for the best ways to explore Australia without breaking the budget? Say hello to the Greyhound Bus, a cost-effective, social, and easy way to travel the country. From surfing waves in the Gold Coast to exploring the country’s rugged outback, you can easily hop from one epic Aussie destination to the next with Greyhound, so here’s everything you need to know before taking your first bus!
![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)
texts.1:
### Greyhound Network and Routes
Greyhound Bus Australia’s network covers all mainland states and territories, connecting major East Coast hotspots with key cities like Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide and Canberra. The network extends to Far North Queensland and even to Alice Springs, the gateway to Australia’s most famous natural landmark; Uluru! With over 180 stops and multiple departures a day on popular routes, it’s easy to find a Greyhound Bus that’s headed for the next Aussie hotspot on your itinerary.
![Image 2](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)
texts.2:
### **Types of Travel Passes**
Greyhound Bus Australia offers a range of different travel passes so you can choose one to best suit your travel needs.
texts.3:
### **Types of Travel Passes**
#### National Whimit Pass
From Far North Queensland to Alice Springs and the East Coast, Greyhound’s National Whimit Pass is the ultimate Australia explorer pass. It allows unlimited travel on Greyhound’s extensive network for a chosen number of days so get ready to head off the beaten track and explore the country’s hidden gems!
texts.4:
### **Types of Travel Passes**
#### East Coast Whimit Pass
The best way to discover Australia’s East Coast is with Greyhound’s most popular East Coast Whimit Pass. This pass offers unlimited travel between Cairns and Melbourne in any direction. You can choose the length of your East Coast pass depending on your travel plans; with popular passes being the 15, 30 and 60-day options. Greyhound also offers additional add-on days if you need to take a few extra buses after your pass has expired!
texts.5:
### **Types of Travel Passes**
#### Create Your Own Pass
If you’re looking for the ultimate flexibility, Greyhound offers a customisable National or East Coast Whimit Pass where you can select the exact number of days you need to travel for.

### Booking and Managing Your Trip
Happy Travels are here to make the booking and managing part of your travels easy. Talk to one of our travel specialists to organise your buses and other travel plans. Our team can also talk you through the process of booking your buses and managing your itinerary, and even how to select a preferred seat on your journeys.
We have created a walkthrough guide of the Greyhound Bus Australia website, explaining how to book your buses and change your seats on the website, which you can view here on our Tiktok. texts.7:
### **Luggage and Travel Assistance**
If you’ve overpacked or accumulated a few souvenirs during your travels, don’t worry! Greyhound Bus Australia allows two pieces of checked baggage with a maximum of 20kg (44lb) and a carry-on bag of up to 8kg. If you have any additional luggage then Greyhound will charge $10 per item and if there is enough room, you can bring your surfboard on the bus for $15 and your bike for $49. Greyhound also offers assistance for travellers needing special accommodations​​ which can be arranged through their Call Centre on 1300 473 946.
texts.8:
### **Top Tips for Travelling with Greyhound**
- Make sure your ID is easily accessible as often it’s required to board the bus.

- The Greyhound Bus stops are often in pretty central locations but you should aim to arrive at the bus stop at least 15 minutes before departure to allow you to check in and put your luggage away.

- If you’re travelling during peak season (November-March) we suggest booking your buses in advance as they can get booked up pretty quickly.

- Most of the buses have built-in USB charging ports so remember to bring a charging cable for your devices with you in your carry-on bag.

- If you’re wanting to save money, Greyhound offers overnight buses on routes such as Sydney to Byron and Airlie Beach to Cairns. With decent legroom, reclining seats, power outlets, wifi and toilets, it’s easy to save a night of accommodation and take a night bus. Waking up somewhere new is pretty epic too.

- The air conditioning might make it a bit chilly on the bus so bring an extra jumper. It can also double up as a pillow to help you get some shut-eye.

- Greyhound offers a bus tracker so you can see your bus in real time, or if someone is meeting you at the stop they can see where you’re at.
